key_facts: Lung cancer is the commonest cause of UK cancer death; skin signs may be the first clue.
**Paraneoplastic**: clubbing/HPOA, dermatomyositis, acanthosis/tripe palms, ectopic ACTH pigmentation.
**Local**: SVC obstruction (facial swelling, distended chest veins), Horner's syndrome; **direct**: skin metastases (chest wall, scalp).
Use smoking history as a red-flag multiplier; refer per NICE NG12. SVC obstruction is same-day.

sections.title: Overview
blocks: Lung cancer is the commonest cause of UK cancer death. Its skin signs are **direct** (metastases), **local** (SVC obstruction, Horner's syndrome), **paraneoplastic** (clubbing/HPOA, dermatomyositis, acanthosis/tripe palms, ectopic ACTH) or **treatment-related** (EGFR-inhibitor acneiform rash, checkpoint-inhibitor rashes, radiotherapy).

ul: **"An acne-like rash on cancer treatment means stop the drug"**: EGFR rashes are managed with oncology protocols and often signal response.

sections.title: Pathophysiology and pathology
blocks: Tumours affect skin through **growth factors, hormones, immunity and spread**.

mech.t: VEGF and PDGF (from platelet clumps bypassing the lung) drive clubbing and HPOA.
Small-cell tumours make ACTH: pigmentation, hypokalaemia.
Anti-tumour immunity cross-reacts with skin and muscle (dermatomyositis).

blocks: Tumour-derived growth factors (TGF-α, EGF, VEGF, PDGF in clubbing/HPOA), ectopic hormones (ACTH — small-cell lung cancer), immune cross-reactivity (DM), haematogenous/lymphatic spread, mechanical obstruction (SVC).

head: Sign
Notes
rows: Loss of the nail-fold angle, Schamroth window lost; HPOA = painful wrists/ankles with periostitis. **NSCLC** especially (adenocarcinoma). Also bronchiectasis, ILD, cyanotic heart disease, IBD, cirrhosis, endocarditis
Firm, painless pink-purple or skin-coloured nodules on the **chest wall, scalp, abdomen/umbilicus**; **carcinoma erysipeloides** (inflammatory, cellulitis-like plaque — photo B01)
Facial/neck oedema and plethora, dilated chest-wall veins, worse lying down — an oncological emergency
Pancoast (apical) tumour: ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis, ± shoulder/arm pain (T1)
Velvety ridged palms; tripe palms alone → lung cancer more likely; with AN → gastric (see *Acanthosis nigricans and PCOS*)
Rapid **hyperpigmentation**, hypokalaemia, myopathy, oedema, hypertension; usually **no time for classic striae**

**Erythema gyratum repens** (rare, wood-grain concentric bands — strongly associated with lung cancer), **acquired hypertrichosis lanuginosa**, sign of **Leser–Trélat** (sudden eruptive seborrhoeic keratoses), **Trousseau's migratory thrombophlebitis**, **Bazex syndrome** (acrokeratosis paraneoplastica — upper aerodigestive SCC, psoriasiform acral plaques), pruritus, Sweet syndrome, paraneoplastic pemphigus, palmar hyperkeratosis

**EGFR inhibitors** (erlotinib, gefitinib, osimertinib): acneiform folliculitis, paronychia, xerosis — doxycycline/lymecycline + topical steroid; **checkpoint inhibitors**: lichenoid/eczematous rashes, vitiligo, bullous pemphigoid, SJS (rare)

ul: **Refer on a suspected cancer pathway** if CXR findings suggest lung cancer, or if aged **≥40 with unexplained haemoptysis**.

**Offer an urgent CXR (within 2 weeks)** to people **≥40** with **two or more** unexplained symptoms — or **one** if they have **ever smoked**: cough, fatigue, shortness of breath, chest pain, weight loss, appetite loss.

**Consider an urgent CXR** in people ≥40 with: persistent or recurrent chest infection; **finger clubbing**; supraclavicular or persistent cervical lymphadenopathy; chest signs consistent with lung cancer; **thrombocytosis**.
Skin metastasis → biopsy (usually via a dermatology urgent pathway) + CT.

sections.title: Differential diagnoses
blocks: Clubbing (above); carcinoma erysipeloides vs **cellulitis** (afebrile, no response to antibiotics, firm); metastases vs cysts/lipomas/DFSP; SVC obstruction vs angioedema/heart failure.

sections.title: Management
blocks: Recognise and refer per NG12. Use **smoking history as a red-flag multiplier**. Smoking cessation support (NCSCT, varenicline/NRT). Manage EGFR-inhibitor rashes with oncology protocols (pre-emptive doxycycline, emollients, SPF, mild steroid).
Recognition, CXR request (where the IP can order it locally), suspected-cancer referral per local IP rights, smoking cessation, supportive dermatology for oncology drug rashes.

refer.t: New finger clubbing, haemoptysis, weight loss or persistent cough in a smoker over 40: **urgent CXR / suspected cancer pathway** (NICE NG12).
‘Cellulitis’ on the chest wall after breast cancer that does not respond to antibiotics: think **carcinoma erysipeloides**, urgent referral.

sections.title: Red flags and when to refer

ul: New finger clubbing, haemoptysis, weight loss or persistent cough in a smoker over 40: **urgent CXR / suspected cancer pathway** (NICE NG12).
‘Cellulitis’ on the chest wall after breast cancer that does not respond to antibiotics: think **carcinoma erysipeloides**, urgent referral.

blocks: SVC obstruction (same day); haemoptysis ≥40 (suspected cancer pathway); new clubbing with chest symptoms; cutaneous nodules in a smoker; rapid pigmentation + hypokalaemia (ectopic ACTH).

pearls: "**Clubbing in a smoker over 40 = chest X-ray.**"
An "**antibiotic-resistant cellulitis**" on the chest wall of a cancer patient may be carcinoma erysipeloides.

quiz.q: When should you think of Skin signs of lung cancer & internal malignancy?
quiz.a: New clubbing, velvety ridged palms, sudden widespread acanthosis nigricans or seborrhoeic keratoses, or a firm red ‘cellulitis’ that does not respond.
Tumour-derived growth factors and cytokines, or direct spread of cancer to the skin.

quiz.q: What is the backbone of care?
quiz.a: Take a smoking and symptom history; CXR and NICE NG12 urgent pathways; don’t keep treating a non-responding ‘cellulitis’.
Lung, gastric and breast cancer; carcinoma erysipeloides mistaken for infection.

quiz.q: Name a red flag that needs escalation.
quiz.a: New finger clubbing, haemoptysis, weight loss or persistent cough in a smoker over 40: **urgent CXR / suspected cancer pathway** (NICE NG12).
